expectations.text: review.md flags that OAuth 2.1 is an Internet-Draft, not RFC 9725 (or any RFC)
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: "OAuth 2.1 has no RFC number. It is the IETF Internet-Draft `draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1`. ... RFC 9725 is a different document."

expectations.text: review.md flags recommending the implicit flow for single-page apps as insecure or removed in OAuth 2.1 / RFC 9700
expectations.evidence: Finding 4: "RFC 9700 ... §2.1.2 says clients SHOULD NOT use the implicit grant" and "The OAuth 2.1 draft removes the implicit grant entirely."

expectations.text: review.md flags storing a long-lived access token in localStorage
expectations.evidence: Finding 5: "30-day access tokens in `localStorage` (line 15). Blocker. Any script on the origin can read `localStorage`, so a single XSS exposes the token."

expectations.text: review.md flags passing the access token as a URL query parameter
expectations.evidence: Finding 6: "Access token in a query parameter (lines 17-21). Blocker. RFC 6750 §2.3 says the URI query method SHOULD NOT be used ... The OAuth 2.1 draft drops the query-parameter method."

expectations.text: review.md questions or flags the "OIDC 2.1 certified" claim as an unverified or nonexistent certification
expectations.evidence: Finding 2: "There is no \"OpenID Connect 2.1\" specification" and "Saying \"is certified\" contradicts the site and is a compliance claim with no evidence behind it."

expectations.text: review.md does not mark the DPoP (RFC 9449) or PKCE (RFC 7636) statements as wrong
expectations.evidence: Finding 7 (line 23, Minor): "The RFC numbers and the summaries are correct." It flags only incompleteness and placement, not correctness.

expectations.text: Each finding in review.md gives a location (line or quoted text), what is wrong, and a fix
expectations.evidence: Findings 1-10 each name lines (e.g. "(line 11)", "(lines 17-21)", "(lines 1-7)") and carry a **Fix:** or example. Finding 7 gives line 23 and implied fixes ("It should be the core of the post", "Say what PKCE protects against"). Finding 11 is located as "all" but quotes `## The standards` and lists concrete actions. Weakest case, still meets the bar.

claims.claim: Frontmatter fails the writing schema: description must be 80-160 chars; headline and lede required
claims.evidence: src/content.config.ts:78 `description: z.string().min(80).max(160)`, :80-81 headline/lede `z.string().min(1)`; the draft's description is 44 characters with no headline/lede.

claims.claim: No web sources were fetched; protocol citations are from memory
claims.evidence: actions.md: "URLs fetched: none"; review header says every citation should be checked against the live spec.

uncertainties: Protocol citations not checked against live specs (no fetch)
PKCE exception section number to be confirmed

suggestions.reason: Add an assertion that citations are verified against primary sources (Datatracker / rfc-editor). That is where the skill run and this run differ. This run cited RFC 9700 and RFC 6750 sections from memory and said so.

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions met. The case does not separate the two configurations.
